original.target_description: Assigned target: honesty-related versus neutral word priming effect on BIDR impression management (IM). Supplied primary paper reports an alcohol-related behavior questionnaire and cheating questions; it does not report this BIDR outcome/test.

n.sample_role: Target BIDR analytic participant N not reported. The 64 undergraduates are the recruitment sample for the alcohol/cheating study, not an established analytic N for this target.
n.exclusions: No target-specific exclusions or final BIDR groups reported.
n.location: p. 323 Participants; p. 324 Dependent measures (PDF pp. 3–4)
n.quote: Sixty-four undergraduates were paid $3.00 ... A two-page ‘‘Health and Education Questionnaire’’

es.location: p. 324 Dependent measures and Results—Composite index (PDF p. 4); p. 325 Order effects and footnote 1
es.quote: A two-page ‘‘Health and Education Questionnaire’’ ... F (1, 62) = 14.05, p < .001.

p.location: p. 324 Dependent measures and Results—Composite index (PDF p. 4); p. 325 Order effects and footnote 1
p.quote: A two-page ‘‘Health and Education Questionnaire’’ ... F (1, 62) = 14.05, p < .001.

notes: The supplied reference title and DOI match the primary paper. The assigned BIDR impression management (IM) target is not a reported measure in this paper. Full supplied text inspected, including Methods, Results, figures, and footnotes; PDF p. 4 rendered and inspected to confirm the two-column layout. Non-target evidence: p. 324 reports F (1, 62) = 14.05, p < .001 for the alcohol-behavior composite, not either BIDR subscale. P. 325 reports order-specific alcohol tests and a cheating comparison, also not BIDR. These are not assigned to any target row. Recruitment of 64 undergraduates does not establish target analytic N; no N derived from degrees of freedom or summed groups. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
